Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
======

## Sprint 1: Review the pull request in pr/

The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (unified diff, base to head). The files before the change are under `pr/base/`, after it under `pr/head/`; `pr/PR.md` is the pull request description and is the implementation report for this sprint.

Read the actual implementation (never documentation alone) and cross-reference the technical-debt registry if one exists. Every finding cites the CWE/OWASP/CVE it violates with an absolute URL (not just the name) and quotes the vulnerable code inline. Where purpose or trust context (internal vs external) is unclear, state the assumption; say "Unable to assess" for obfuscated or inaccessible code and record scope limits in the report.
</grounding_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. Blockers: an unverified missing report; uncommented security-critical code; a CHANGELOG omitting security changes; secrets or internal URLs in docs or comments; auth/crypto changes without security documentation; API changes that don't match the endpoint docs.
</documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.
</checklists>

<beads_workflow>
With `br` installed: `resources/BEADS-WORKFLOW.md` (sync, the audit comment, the `security*` labels, a discovered vulnerability).
</beads_workflow>

<retrospective_postlude>
<!-- @skill-include: start retrospective_postlude | hash:53d44248 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md -->
After the main skill logic, if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled`
prints `true` (and `invisible_retrospective.skills` does not disable this skill), silently run the
learning-signal scan per `.claude/skills/continuous-learning/SKILL.md` and its

# Task: review a pull request

The directory `pr/` holds one pull request against a repository of shell scripts, tests and documentation, frozen for evaluation. The change: sprint-256 — inert controls repaired or retired, file-authoritative run position, fail-closed heredoc classifier, profiles, prose-diet fallback.

The pull request is laid out as:

- `pr/PR.md` — the title and description
- `pr/head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base to head)
- `pr/base/` — every touched file before the change
- `pr/head/` — every touched file after the change

Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for the repository: find the defects it introduces and decide whether it can merge. Do not change any file under `pr/`.

Write your review to `review.md` at the repository root (a review workflow that also writes its own report files may do so; `review.md` follows this shape regardless):

- one finding per line, in the form `head/<path>:<line> — <description>`, where `<path>` is the file's path under `pr/head/` and `<line>` is a line number in that file;

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. ## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md (Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`, cycle-129 sprint-256, 68 files)
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (carries only the PR title and file count)

---

## Overall Assessment

The PR delivers five pieces. It adds implement-gate modes (`ask | telemetry | deny`) and a file-derived run position (`run-checkpoint.sh derive / record-round / mark / unmark`). It adds a heredoc consumer classifier to the destructive-command fence and a `loa.profile` resolver (`profile-lib.sh`) that every knob reader now uses. It also moves the Agent Teams table out of the kernel.

Much of it is solid. The new implement-gate matrix (IG-24 to IG-33) passes on this host. The deny reply follows the PreToolUse contract, and trust-input writes ask in every mode. The profile resolver handles an explicit `false`, floor keys and a missing profiles file correctly. The fence corpus passes every benign row and every dangerous row.

Three defects block the merge:

1. **The fence classifier is not fail-closed.** Some commands that the base hook blocks are now allowed. The primary dissent voice found the same class on its own (DISS-001).
2. **`run-checkpoint.sh derive` fails on jq 1.6.** It uses `$label` as a jq variable name, which is reserved in jq 1.6, so it never writes `derived_at`. With that missing, the whole FR-5 feature is inert on any host with jq 1.6.
3. **`record-round` crashes on legacy feedback with no trailer** under jq 1.6.

On top of that, the implementation report has no `## AC Verification` section, which triggers CHANGES_REQUIRED automatically under this skill.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security: the heredoc classifier lets a body through when the same command later executes it

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608-640` — `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` decides whether a heredoc's target file is executed later in the same command. It only looks at the command word of the segment that names the file (line 631). It does not look at where that segment's output goes. A safe reader whose output reaches an interpreter on another line of the same command therefore leaves the heredoc `nonexec`. `_bdb_hd_scan_body` (`:576-604`) then drops the body lines. The fence (`:1062-1063`) never sees the destructive text, and the call is allowed.

**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608-640`
**Issue:** I replayed seven crafted commands of this class through both hooks in a scratch directory. The base hook blocked all seven. The head hook allowed five, and the two it still blocks are the shapes the corpus already covers. The header comment and `head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:294` both promise that naming the target elsewhere "outside a safe reader" forces a full scan. That promise does not hold once the reader's output feeds an interpreter. This is a regression against the base fence, not a gap it already had.
**Why This Matters:** The fence is the only check on destructive Bash for autonomous agents (CWE-184, incomplete list of disallowed inputs). The PR presents this classifier as fail-closed.
**Required Fix:** If any other line of the command names the heredoc's target, judge that line's whole pipeline or statement, not just the segment's command word. That covers pipe targets, a command substitution or `eval`, and a glob that can match the target. Any interpreter or runner anywhere on such a line should force `interpreter` class. The simplest fail-closed version: if any line outside the heredoc holds an interpreter word, a substitution or an unquoted glob, fall back to a full scan. Add corpus `D` rows for each pipeline and substitution shape, and re-run `run-corpus.sh --knob-off --rows` against the base hook to confirm nothing goes from blocked to allowed.
**Reference:** OWASP ASVS V5 (input validation, deny by default); CWE-184.

### 2. Functionality: `derive` cannot compile its jq program on jq 1.6

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378-380` — the per-sprint jq program binds `--arg label` and reads `$label`. In jq 1.6 `label` is a keyword, so the call fails to compile and `cmd_derive` exits 3 under `set -e`.

**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378-389`
**Issue:** The failure reproduces here (jq 1.6):

```
jq: error: syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__ ... line 2:
      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
```

Running the PR's own `tests/unit/run-checkpoint-derive.bats` on a head overlay tree fails 13 of 22 cases (RCD-1 to RCD-12 and RCD-14), all with this error. Every caller hides it. `write` and `mark` swallow derive failures (lines 174 and 541), `loa-status.sh` discards stderr, and `halt-resume.md` step 0a treats a non-zero exit as no drift. As a result, `derived_at` is never written, and `implement_gate.mode: deny` always falls back to ask with "cache not derived". The breaker is never recomputed and `/loa` never prints the Run line.
**Required Fix:** Rename the variable (for example `--arg lbl` and `$lbl` at lines 378, 380 and 389). Add a CI job, or a bats `setup` guard, that runs the suite under jq 1.6. Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 still ship jq 1.6.

### 3. Functionality: `record-round` crashes on a feedback file without a trailer

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:224-226` — for a feedback file without an `LOA-VERDICT` trailer, `tl` is empty and `pj` becomes an empty string. On jq 1.6, `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<""` exits 0, so the `|| pj='{}'` fallback never fires. `jq --argjson p ""` at line 232 then aborts with "invalid JSON text passed to --argjson", and `record-round` exits 2.

**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:224-232`
**Issue:** This reproduces outside bats on a trailer-less review file. `tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats` RCR-7 fails for this reason. The run-mode skill (`head/.claude/skills/run-mode/SKILL.md:110`) now sends every review and audit round through `record-round`. On jq 1.6, a legacy-format round therefore stops the run loop where it should count as findings. The same empty-input guard is used at line 223 for `vj`, and `rounds_of` and `derive` reach `fb_parse` too.
**Required Fix:** Test for non-empty input before the type check, for example `[[ -n "$pj" ]] && jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj" >/dev/null 2>&1 || pj='{}'`, and do the same for `vj`. Add a bats case that runs a trailer-less file under jq 1.6.

---

## Observations

### 1. Skill allowlists

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:6` — the regenerated includes at lines 69 and 297 tell the skill to run `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob …`. The `allowed-tools` line has no `Bash(.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob *)` grant, and `deny_raw_shell: true` is set. The harness refuses the call, so the guardrail check and the retrospective postlude never run. **Suggestion:** Add the grant to both frontmatters and their `capabilities.execute_commands`. Have `validate-skill-capabilities.sh` check that every command an include tells the skill to run is in its allowlist.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:558-569` — `read_position` treats the position as known whenever `derived_at` is fresh, and it never looks at `timestamps.last_activity`. A RUNNING cache whose activity stamp is older than 24 hours gets no sanction from `check_implementation_active` (line 505). It is still denied, with the self-contradicting reason "derived position: RUNNING". This reproduces with `run_mode.stale_hours: 48` and `last_activity` 30 hours old. Matches DISS-C-001.
- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:545-552` — the marker sanction expires 7200 seconds after `started_at`, and nothing refreshes it (`run-checkpoint.sh write` does not touch the marker). **Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md (Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`, cycle-129 sprint-256, 68 files)

## Overall Assessment

The PR delivers five pieces. It adds implement-gate modes (`ask | telemetry | deny`) and a file-derived run position (`run-checkpoint.sh derive / record-round / mark / unmark`). It adds a heredoc consumer classifier to the destructive-command fence and a `loa.profile` resolver (`profile-lib.sh`) that every knob reader now uses. It also moves the Agent Teams table out of the kernel.

Much of it is solid. The new implement-gate matrix (IG-24 to IG-33) passes on this host. The deny reply follows the PreToolUse contract, and trust-input writes ask in every mode. The profile resolver handles an explicit `false`, floor keys and a missing profiles file correctly. The fence corpus passes every benign row and every dangerous row.

Three defects block the merge:

1. **The fence classifier is not fail-closed.** Some commands that the base hook blocks are now allowed. The primary dissent voice found the same class on its own (DISS-001).
2. **`run-checkpoint.sh derive` fails on jq 1.6.** It uses `$label` as a jq variable name, which is reserved in jq 1.6, so it never writes `derived_at`. With that missing, the whole FR-5 feature is inert on any host with jq 1.6.
3. **`record-round` crashes on legacy feedback with no trailer** under jq 1.6.

On top of that, the implementation report has no `## AC Verification` section, which triggers CHANGES_REQUIRED automatically under this skill.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

## Changes Required

### 1. Security: the heredoc classifier lets a body through when the same command later executes it

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608-640` — `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` decides whether a heredoc's target file is executed later in the same command. It only looks at the command word of the segment that names the file (line 631). It does not look at where that segment's output goes. A safe reader whose output reaches an interpreter on another line of the same command therefore leaves the heredoc `nonexec`. `_bdb_hd_scan_body` (`:576-604`) then drops the body lines. The fence (`:1062-1063`) never sees the destructive text, and the call is allowed.

**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608-640`
**Issue:** I replayed seven crafted commands of this class through both hooks in a scratch directory. The base hook blocked all seven. The head hook allowed five, and the two it still blocks are the shapes the corpus already covers. The header comment and `head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:294` both promise that naming the target elsewhere "outside a safe reader" forces a full scan. That promise does not hold once the reader's output feeds an interpreter. This is a regression against the base fence, not a gap it already had.
**Why This Matters:** The fence is the only check on destructive Bash for autonomous agents (CWE-184, incomplete list of disallowed inputs). The PR presents this classifier as fail-closed.
**Required Fix:** If any other line of the command names the heredoc's target, judge that line's whole pipeline or statement, not just the segment's command word. That covers pipe targets, a command substitution or `eval`, and a glob that can match the target. Any interpreter or runner anywhere on such a line should force `interpreter` class. The simplest fail-closed version: if any line outside the heredoc holds an interpreter word, a substitution or an unquoted glob, fall back to a full scan. Add corpus `D` rows for each pipeline and substitution shape, and re-run `run-corpus.sh --knob-off --rows` against the base hook to confirm nothing goes from blocked to allowed.
**Reference:** OWASP ASVS V5 (input validation, deny by default); CWE-184.

### 2. Functionality: `derive` cannot compile its jq program on jq 1.6

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378-380` — the per-sprint jq program binds `--arg label` and reads `$label`. In jq 1.6 `label` is a keyword, so the call fails to compile and `cmd_derive` exits 3 under `set -e`.

**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378-389`
**Issue:** The failure reproduces here (jq 1.6):

```
jq: error: syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__ ... line 2:
      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
```

Running the PR's own `tests/unit/run-checkpoint-derive.bats` on a head overlay tree fails 13 of 22 cases (RCD-1 to RCD-12 and RCD-14), all with this error. Every caller hides it. `write` and `mark` swallow derive failures (lines 174 and 541), `loa-status.sh` discards stderr, and `halt-resume.md` step 0a treats a non-zero exit as no drift. As a result, `derived_at` is never written, and `implement_gate.mode: deny` always falls back to ask with "cache not derived". The breaker is never recomputed and `/loa` never prints the Run line.
**Required Fix:** Rename the variable (for example `--arg lbl` and `$lbl` at lines 378, 380 and 389). Add a CI job, or a bats `setup` guard, that runs the suite under jq 1.6. Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 still ship jq 1.6.

### 3. Functionality: `record-round` crashes on a feedback file without a trailer

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:224-226` — for a feedback file without an `LOA-VERDICT` trailer, `tl` is empty and `pj` becomes an empty string. On jq 1.6, `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<""` exits 0, so the `|| pj='{}'` fallback never fires. `jq --argjson p ""` at line 232 then aborts with "invalid JSON text passed to --argjson", and `record-round` exits 2.

**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:224-232`
**Issue:** This reproduces outside bats on a trailer-less review file. `tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats` RCR-7 fails for this reason. The run-mode skill (`head/.claude/skills/run-mode/SKILL.md:110`) now sends every review and audit round through `record-round`. On jq 1.6, a legacy-format round therefore stops the run loop where it should count as findings. The same empty-input guard is used at line 223 for `vj`, and `rounds_of` and `derive` reach `fb_parse` too.
**Required Fix:** Test for non-empty input before the type check, for example `[[ -n "$pj" ]] && jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj" >/dev/null 2>&1 || pj='{}'`, and do the same for `vj`. Add a bats case that runs a trailer-less file under jq 1.6.

_bdb_hd_segword() {

  while (( guard < 64 )); do

# is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
# under a caller's `set -u`.
#
# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
# =============================================================================
_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'
_bdb_hd_re_ext='\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|csh|fish|py|pyw|rb|pl|pm|js|mjs|cjs|ts|mts|cts|ps1|psm1|php|lua|tcl|command|bat|cmd)$'
_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'
_bdb_hd_re_rc='(^|/)\.(bashrc|bash_profile|bash_login|bash_logout|profile|zshrc|zshenv|zprofile|zlogin|zlogout|kshrc|mkshrc|cshrc|tcshrc|login|logout|envrc)$'
_bdb_hd_re_sedp='^(([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/)(,([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/))?)?p$'
_bdb_hd_re_assign='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*='
_bdb_hd_re_varw='^[$]([{]|[A-Za-z_])'
_bdb_hd_re_knob='^[[:space:]]+heredoc_classifier:[[:space:]]*["'"'"']?([A-Za-z]+)["'"'"']?[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$'

# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
  case "$1" in
    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;
    sudo|doas|su|runuser|env|xargs|parallel|timeout|nohup|nice|ionice|setsid|stdbuf|chroot|unshare|nsenter|ssh|docker|podman|kubectl|find|watch|script) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
  case "$1" in
    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
# Command words the fence's own rules match.
_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {
  case "$1" in
    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;
    [Dd][Rr][Oo][Pp]|[Dd][Ee][Ll][Ee][Tt][Ee]|[Tt][Rr][Uu][Nn][Cc][Aa][Tt][Ee]) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
# Readers that may name a heredoc's target elsewhere on the line.
_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {
  case "$1" in
    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
  n=${#s}
  _bdb_hd_tok=()
  while (( i < n )); do
    ch="${s:i:1}"
    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
      tok="$tok$ch"
      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
        q=""
      fi
      i=$((i + 1)); continue
    fi
    case "$ch" in
      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      '\')
        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
      ' '|$'\t')
        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      '#')
        (( have )) || return 1
        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
        op=""
        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
        done
        i=$((i + ${#op}))
        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
        fi
        if (( have )); then
          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
            op="$tok$op"
          else
            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
          fi
          tok=""; have=0
        fi
        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
    esac
  done
  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
  return 0
}

# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
  _hd_up=""
  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
    _hd_up="$1"
  else
    return 1
  fi
  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
}

# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
# content (or cannot be judged).
_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {

# =============================================================================
# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
# under a caller's `set -u`.
#
# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
# =============================================================================
_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'

_bdb_hd_is_interp() {

# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators

# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
  n=${#s}
  _bdb_hd_tok=()
  while (( i < n )); do
    ch="${s:i:1}"
    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
      tok="$tok$ch"
      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
        q=""
      fi
      i=$((i + 1)); continue
    fi
    case "$ch" in
      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      '\')
        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
      ' '|$'\t')
        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      '#')
        (( have )) || return 1
        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
        op=""
        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
        done
        i=$((i + ${#op}))
        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
        fi
        if (( have )); then
          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
            op="$tok$op"
          else
            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
          fi
          tok=""; have=0
        fi
        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
    esac
  done
  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"

# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable

_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {

# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
fb_parse() {
  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
  else
    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
  fi
  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
----
    mex=false; msid=""
    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
      mex=true
      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
    fi
    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \
              --argjson mex "$mex" --arg msid "$msid" --arg ic "$ic" '
      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
----
        plan_id=$(jq -r '.plan_id // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || true

        # Integrity: must have plan_id
        if [[ -z "$plan_id" ]]; then
            return 1
        fi

        # Integrity: check staleness (within 24 h either side, via _ig_fresh); an absent or unparsable
        # last_activity is stale too (sprint-250 audit LOW-006: the check was skipped, so RUNNING + plan_id allowed)
        last_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || last_activity=""

            return 1  # Stale, future-dated or unstamped state
        fi

        if ! _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json"; then
            return 1
        fi

        if [[ "$state" == "RUNNING" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Check simstim state; its writers (simstim-state.sh, simstim-orchestrator.sh) stamp .timestamps.last_activity,
    # and a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" ]]; then
        local phase simstim_activity
        phase=$(jq -r '.phase // empty' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        simstim_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || simstim_activity=""
        if [[ "$phase" == "implementation" ]] && _ig_fresh "$simstim_activity"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Check run state; run-mode stamps .timestamps.last_activity (state-schemas.md), .updated_at is the fallback
    # run-preflight.sh reads too; a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/state.json" ]]; then
        local run_state run_activity
        run_state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        run_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // .updated_at // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || run_activity=""
        if [[ "$run_state" == "RUNNING" ]] && _ig_fresh "$run_activity" && _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/state.json"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    return 1
}

# The implementing skills' marker (run-checkpoint.sh mark): 0 fresh and well-formed, 1 absent, 2 stale or malformed
check_implement_marker() {
    local f="$RUN_DIR/implement-active.json" started
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 1
    jq -e '(.skill == "implement" or .skill == "bug") and (.sprint | type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$"))' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
    started=$(jq -r '.started_at // empty | strings' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || started=""
    _ig_within 7200 "$started" || return 2
    return 0
}

# The derived run position for deny: known only when .run/sprint-plan-state.json parses and carries a derived_at
# within run_mode.stale_hours; sets position_state (display copy) or position_why
position_state=""
position_why=""
read_position() {
    local f="$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" da st
    if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then position_why="cache missing"; return 1; fi
    if ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then position_why="cache unparseable"; return 1; fi
    da=$(jq -r '.derived_at // empty | strings' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || da=""
    if [[ -z "$da" ]]; then position_why="cache not derived"; return 1; fi
    if ! _ig_within $(( gate_stale_hours * 3600 )) "$da"; then position_why="cache older than run_mode.stale_hours"; return 1; fi
    st=$(jq -r '.state // .status // empty | strings' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || st=""
    position_state=$(strip_controls "${st:-unknown}")
    [[ -n "$position_state" ]] || position_state="unknown"
    return 0
}

emit_deny() {
    jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
}
deny_reason() {
    printf 'App Zone write with no active implementation run (derived position: %s); run /implement or /bug, or set implement_gate.mode: ask' "$position_state"
}

sanction=""
if check_implementation_active; then

else

    elif [[ "${LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE:-}" == "1" ]]; then

input.content:
# Security Audit: sprint-1 (PR cycle-129 sprint-256)

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Task:** review-r20
**Scope:** `pr/head.diff` (68 files). Base files are in `pr/base/`, head files in `pr/head/`. The implementation report is `pr/PR.md`, mirrored in `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md`.
**Review gate input:** `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md` (verdict CHANGES_REQUIRED, excluded 0)

## Verdict

**CHANGES_REQUIRED**

The tally has four high findings, and any high forces this verdict. The heredoc classifier fails open against shapes the base fence blocked. Two run-position paths crash on jq 1.6. The default profile silently turns off two security controls that used to default on.

## Prerequisites and scope limits

- **Review gate not passed.** Phase 0 requires `engineer-feedback.md` to say "All good". It says CHANGES_REQUIRED with three high findings. Normally the audit would stop here. The phase instruction requires a feedback file, so the audit ran in full and this report records the result.
- **Adversarial review present.** `adversarial-review.json` carries `metadata.model: gpt-5.5-pro`, as the gate requires.
- **Integrity pre-check.** `detect-drift.sh` reports no significant drift. `integrity_enforcement` is not set in `.loa.config.yaml`.
- **Input guardrails.** The orchestrator returned `PROCEED`.
- **Scope script.** `security-audit-scope.sh` scans the installed repository, not the frozen PR, so the PR files were catalogued by hand. The diff touches System Zone hooks, scripts, skills, tests and one CI workflow. It does not touch `src/`, `lib/` or `app/`.
- **No live replay of fence bypasses.** The classifier findings come from reading the code paths, not from running crafted destructive payloads.
- **Not assessed.** The reviewer reported that the PF-5 floor test in `head/tests/unit/profile-floor.bats:141` fails. This audit did not reproduce it, and it is not tallied here.
- **Host.** jq 1.6, bats and yq are installed.

## Security dissenter analysis (Phase 1C)

`adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id sprint-1 --diff-file pr/head.diff --json` finished with status `reviewed`. The primary voice was gpt-5.5-pro. The companion voice, claude-headless, succeeded and counted as an independent voice. The run reports `degraded: false` with no degraded-security-review marker. It wrote `adversarial-audit.json` with eight findings, and `adversarial-rejected-audit.jsonl` is empty.

- **Reference.** CWE-345, Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html
- **Remediation.** Bind the marker to the session, for example with a session id from the hook payload. Name the path explicitly in the accepted-gap list in `hooks-reference.md`.

The audit verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The feedback file is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`, and the verdict checker reports its prose and trailer as consistent.

The review gate had not passed. The reviewer's verdict was CHANGES_REQUIRED, not "All good", which normally stops an audit. The task required a feedback file, so I ran the full audit and recorded that in the report.

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 4 |
| Medium | 4 |
| Low | 4 |

**High findings:**
- **The heredoc classifier lets dangerous commands through.** It drops a heredoc body when a later pipeline stage or a glob runs the file it wrote. The base fence blocked these shapes. This is in `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:612` and lines 626 to 631. I confirmed it by reading the code and did not run attack payloads.
- **The run-position step breaks on jq 1.6.** It uses `$label` as a jq variable, which jq 1.6 reserves. The cache stamp is never written, so deny mode never takes effect. This is at `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378-380`, and I reproduced it on this host.
- **Recording a round crashes on old-format feedback under jq 1.6.** A feedback file with no verdict trailer aborts the run loop, at `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:224-232`. I reproduced this too.
- **The default profile silently turns off two security controls.** Input guardrails and danger-level enforcement both used to default on. Under the default profile they are now off, with no changelog entry or upgrade warning. This is at `head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:40-41`.

**Medium findings:**
- **Two gate skills lack a permission they need.** The audit and review skills tell themselves to run the profile knob reader, but their allowlists do not grant it.
- **Deny mode can block a legitimate run.** It rejects a running session with a contradictory "RUNNING" reason when the activity stamp is old.
- **The implement marker expires after two hours.** Nothing refreshes it, so long sessions start asking or getting denied.
- **The model can grant itself the implement marker.** It can create the marker through Bash, which unlocks two hours of silent writes even in the default mode.

The independent dissent review finished and was not degraded. It raised eight findings and had no rejected payloads. I confirmed or merged six of them, downgraded the team-rules one, and dismissed the config-path one because turning that setting off only makes the fence stricter.

The test parse error the reviewer reported is already in the base snapshot, so I did not count it against this PR. One floor test the reviewer saw fail was not reproduced and is not counted.
